title: Agendas, Board Papers and Information Quality
summary: How the agenda, the quality of papers and the volume of information shape what the board actually scrutinises, and what good and poor board information look like.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How the agenda, the quality of papers and the volume of information shape what the board actually scrutinises, and what good and poor board information look like.
Learning Objectives: Assess whether the agenda gives proper time to strategic and risk issues
Distinguish a decision-ready board paper from narrative without a clear ask
Evaluate whether management information is concise, prioritised and exception-based
Syllabus: Agenda curation, routine reporting and items carried over or pushed to the end
Good papers: decision required, options, recommendation, risks and prior challenge
Information overload and the shortcuts overwhelmed boards take
Supervisory questions to test papers and information quality
Intended Audience: Supervisors and governance specialists who assess boards and senior management of regulated firms
Staff conducting fit and proper, governance or culture reviews and interviewing chairs and directors
Senior supervisors and team leaders who review governance assessments and decide the supervisory response
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of governance assessment or supervisory interviews is helpful. No board experience is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Corporate Governance Principles for Banks (2015)
FSB, Guidance on Supervisory Interaction with Financial Institutions on Risk Culture (2014)
Amy C. Edmondson, The Fearless Organization: Creating Psychological Safety in the Workplace (2018)
